items.abstract: <jats:p>Post-zygotically acquired mosaic variants contribute to a range of neurological disorders, yet the cell types that harbor these variants and the role of the variant cells in disease pathophysiology remain unclear. We developed Somatic-Mosaicism-Sequencing (SoMoSeq), a single-nucleus workflow that enables locus-specific DNA genotyping or genome-wide sequencing alongside full-length transcriptome profiling in human brain tissue. This approach maps variant distribution across cell types, linking each nucleus’s genotype directly to its transcriptional profile. We applied SoMoSeq to 1,116 single nuclei from surgically resected brain tissue of three individuals with known mosaic PIK3CA- or SLC35A2-associated focal malformations of cortical development and autopsy brain tissue of five control individuals. The workflow achieved reproducible genotype assignment with assay-dependent call rates of 60-80%, resolved major cortical cell classes from the matched transcriptomes, and generated deep transcriptional profiles from selected genotyped nuclei. Integrating genotype with gene expression revealed cell-type-specific distributions of pathogenic variants and enabled genotype-resolved interrogation of transcriptional states. Together, SoMoSeq provides a platform for integrated analysis of mosaic variant cellular distribution and genotype-linked transcriptional states in human brain tissue.  ​</jats:p>
title: Somatic Mosaicism Sequencing (SoMoSeq): A method for genotype-informed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of mosaic brain tissue
